paper_title: Precision Metrology Meets Cosmology: Improved Constraints on Ultralight Dark Matter from Atom-Cavity Frequency Comparisons
coupling_convention: dimensionless d_me (modulus of coupling to electron mass)
notes: Atom-cavity frequency comparison (Sr optical clock, cryogenic Si cavity, H maser) constraining dilatonic ultralight dark matter coupling. Paper sets NEW limits on BOTH the fine-structure-constant modulus d_e (ScalarPhoton, Fig 2a, from Sr/Si and H/Si) and the electron-mass modulus d_me (ScalarElectron, Fig 2b, from H/Si). Per hint I report the d_me (ScalarElectron) result. Text states improvement by up to a factor 100 between 2e-19 and 2e-21 eV, disfavoring d_me at ~4e-5 for the lowest masses (~2e-21 eV). Numerical values are approximate, read/inferred from text and Fig 2(b) axes (no data table given); the limit is mass-dependent (grows with mass). 95% CL. Local DM density assumed 0.3 GeV/cm^3 (Eq. 6). Confidence limited by (a) paper constrains two coupling types and (b) only approximate text/plot values available.
